PyTorch diagnostics should isolate randomness and restore model state. Use dedicated seeded NumPy/PyTorch generators; if a probe consumes global PyTorch randomness, `torch.random.fork_rng` restores CPU and specified GPU RNG states afterward. Save training flags, call `view.model.eval()`, run ranking probes under `torch.inference_mode()`, and restore flags in `finally`. Inference mode alone does not disable dropout. Gradient-based probes require a separate gradient-enabled context. Sources: [RNG isolation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/random.html), [inference mode](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.autograd.grad_mode.inference_mode.html).

For sampled diagnostics, recommended implementation: cache fixed per-user candidates, sampling negatives without replacement from eligible items after excluding padding, observed history and the positive target. NumPy supports this through `Generator.choice(..., replace=False)`. Keep diagnostic samples separate from the pinned host evaluation; seed=42 alone does not reproduce an evaluator with different sampling order or RNG implementation. Label sampled metrics explicitly, retaining the host’s 99-negative, 200-user/category macro HR@10 for selection. [NumPy sampling](https://numpy.org/doc/1.25/reference/random/generated/numpy.random.Generator.choice.html).

For the required 20 training-user recommendations, recommended implementation: encode each history once, score every item in its category in chunks, exclude all seen items and padding, and merge chunk winners into an exact running top-k. This bounds score-buffer memory while still scoring the complete catalog. Apply the same deterministic tie rule at every pruning and merge step, such as score descending then item ID ascending. PyTorch warns that `topk` tied indices are unstable; stable sorting preserves a predetermined secondary order. Never return masked items when fewer than k eligible items remain. Sources: [topk](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.topk.html), [stable sorting](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.sort.html).
